blocks.text: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ would sit on the floor, eat on the floor, hold down a goat himself while milking it and even accept the invitation of a slave to partake of barley bread." Another narration states that even in the middle of the night Rasulullaah ﷺ would accept the invitation to eat barley bread extended by a person from the upper part of Madinah."[^1]

Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ would accept an invitation even if it were to eat barley bread and foul-smelling fat. Rasulullaah ﷺ also had a suit of armour that he pawned to a Jew and until the day he passed away, he did not have enough money to recover the armour from the man.[^2]
A Narration of Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA)
Hadhrat Umar (RA) says that when a man called for Rasulullaah ﷺ three times, Rasulullaah ﷺ replied with the word "Labbaik" ('At your service') each time.[^3]
The Incident of Rasulullaah ﷺ with a Woman

Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) narrates that (during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ) there was an immoral woman who was flirtatious with the men. She once passed by Rasulullaah ﷺ when he was busy eating Thareed. She shouted out, "Look at this man, sitting like a slave and eating like a slave!" Rasulullaah ﷺ remarked, "Which slave can be more devoted in his servitude (to Allaah) than I?" She then said further, "He eats without giving me anything to eat." "Do eat," Rasulullaah ﷺ said. "Give me with your hand," she demanded. When Rasulullaah ﷺ gave her, she made a further demand saying, "Give me from what is in your mouth." When Rasulullaah ﷺ complied and she ate the food, (its blessings were so profound that) the woman was overcome with modesty and she never flirted with a man for the rest of her life.[^4]
The Incident of Rasulullaah ﷺ with a Man who was Shivering before him

Hadhrat Jareer (RA) reports that when a man once came before Rasulullaah ﷺ, he started to shiver. Rasulullaah ﷺ put him at ease saying, "Take it easy. I am not a king but merely the son of a woman from the Quraysh who used to eat dried meat."[^5]

Another narration[^6] from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) states that it was on the day the Muslims conquered Makkah that a man started shivering while talking to Rasulullaah ﷺ. The rest of the narration is like the one above.
